Declaration by the customer in the application form would suffice for classifying credit facilities to Minorities/SCs/STs under Weaker Sections

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the co-lending model (CLM) between banks and NBFCs for priority sector loans, based on RBI's PSL FAQs (September 2026):
I. If the bank can exercise its discretion on taking the NBFC-originated loans into its books, the arrangement is akin to a direct assignment transaction.
II. If the agreement entails a prior, irrevocable commitment by the bank to take its share of each loan, the arrangement is also akin to a direct assignment transaction.
III. The bilateral Master Agreement may cap the number and amount of loans the NBFC can originate under the CLM.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say only an arrangement in which the bank can exercise discretion over taking the loans is akin to direct assignment; a prior, irrevocable commitment is not. The Master Agreement governs the arrangement and may specify a cap on the number and amount of loans.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: Only if the bank can exercise its discretion regarding taking into its books the loans originated by NBFC as per the agreement, the arrangement will be akin to a direct assignment transaction. If the Agreement entails a prior, irrevocable commitment ... it shall not be akin to direct assignment transaction
The agreement may specify any cap on the number and amount of loans that can be originated by the NBFC under the Co-lending model

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Does a scheduled commercial bank need RBI's permission in each case to open a Banking Outlet in a Tier 1 centre, under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025?

options.text: No; banks have general permission to open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres unless specifically restricted
Yes; permission is needed for every outlet in any centre
No, but only if the outlet is manned by a Business Correspondent
Yes; permission is needed for every outlet in Tier 1 and Tier 2 centres

solution.explanation: With financial inclusion as the overarching objective, a scheduled commercial bank may open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres without RBI permission in each case, unless specifically restricted; a bank from which general permission has been withdrawn needs prior approval.
steps: Exception: bank whose general permission is withdrawn
solution.why_others_wrong: Case-by-case permission is not required in any tier, and the permission is not limited to BC-manned outlets.
solution.final_answer: Option A: No; banks have general permission to open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres unless specifically restricted

fact_checks.claim: a scheduled commercial bank is permitted to open Banking Outlets in Tier 1 to Tier 6 centres without having the need to obtain permission from RBI in each case, unless otherwise specifically restricted

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: When RBI introduced the Business Correspondent model, banks could not collect any charges from customers for services delivered through BCs. According to RBI's discussion paper on engaging 'for-profit' companies as BCs, when were banks first allowed to collect reasonable service charges for such services?

solution.explanation: RBI's discussion paper records that, initially, banks were not allowed to collect charges for BC services; in November 2009 they were allowed to collect reasonable service charges from customers in a transparent manner under a Board-approved policy. (Today the bank, not the BC, may levy such charges.)
solution.why_others_wrong: January 2006 is when the BC model began; April 2008 brought the base-branch rules; September 2010 widened the list of eligible BCs.

fact_checks.claim: Initially, banks were not allowed to collect any charges from the customers for providing services through BC ... Subsequently, banks were allowed in November 2009 to collect reasonable service charges from customers in a transparent manner under a Board-approved policy

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to SBI's FAQs on PMJDY, how did Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana differ from the earlier Financial Inclusion Plan ('Swabhimaan')?

options.text: Swabhimaan offered overdrafts, whereas PMJDY offers none
Swabhimaan focused on covering villages, whereas PMJDY covers rural and urban areas, aiming at every household/adult
Swabhimaan was run by RBI, whereas PMJDY is run by NABARD
Swabhimaan covered only urban areas, whereas PMJDY covers only rural areas

solution.explanation: SBI's FAQs explain that the earlier plan focused on coverage of villages, while PMJDY covers both rural and urban areas and extends banking to households and, after its extension, to every unbanked adult.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swabhimaan was not urban-only; PMJDY does offer an overdraft; PMJDY is run by the Department of Financial Services, not NABARD.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Swabhimaan focused on covering villages, whereas PMJDY covers rural and urban areas, aiming at every household/adult

fact_checks.claim: PMJDY focuses on coverage of 'every adults' as against the earlier plan which focused on coverage of villages. It focuses on coverage of rural as well as urban areas

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank uses its Business Correspondents for preliminary work in opening customer accounts. Under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, who is responsible for ensuring compliance with KYC and AML norms in the BC model?

options.text: The base Banking Outlet's local Lead District Manager

solution.concept: KYC responsibility in the BC model
solution.explanation: KYC and AML procedures under RBI's KYC Directions must be followed in all cases. The bank may use the BC for preliminary account-opening work, but ensuring KYC/AML compliance under the BC model remains the bank's responsibility.
solution.why_others_wrong: Responsibility is not shifted to the BC, the LDM or UIDAI.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the history of the Business Correspondent model, as recorded in RBI's discussion paper on engaging 'for-profit' companies as BCs:
I. Guidelines of April 2008 required every BC to be attached to a base branch, ordinarily within 15 km in rural, semi-urban and urban areas and 5 km in metropolitan centres.
II. The Committee on Financial Inclusion (Chairman: Dr C. Rangarajan) observed that NBFCs engaged in micro finance could be recognised as BCs only for savings and remittance services.
III. From the start of the BC model in 2006, banks could levy service charges on customers for services rendered through BCs.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: The April 2008 guideline attached each BC to a base branch, ordinarily within 15 km (rural, semi-urban, urban) or 5 km (metropolitan). The Rangarajan Committee observed that micro-finance NBFCs could be BCs only for savings and remittance services, where there is no conflict of interest. Charges were not allowed at first; reasonable charges were permitted only from November 2009.
steps: III: wrong (charges allowed only from November 2009)
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

The Committee on Financial Inclusion (Chairman: Dr C. Rangarajan) had observed that NBFCs engaged in micro finance could be recognized as BCs of banks for providing only savings and remittance services
Initially, banks were not allowed to collect any charges ... Subsequently, banks were allowed in November 2009 to collect reasonable service charges

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about grievance redressal and social audit in the Business Correspondent model under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025:
I. As a measure of social audit, there could be periodic block-level meetings of the public with BCs and linked branch managers, which the Lead District Manager could attend.
II. The bank must widely publicise the name and contact number of its designated Grievance Redressal Officer for complaints about BC services.
III. Complaints about services rendered by BCs are to be redressed by the BC company's own grievance machinery, not the bank's.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: The Directions suggest periodic block-level meetings as social audit, which the LDM could attend to get feedback. Grievance redressal machinery for BC services must be constituted within the bank and publicised, with the designated officer's name and number made known. Statement III is wrong.
steps: III: wrong (machinery is within the bank)
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing III are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) rules, what Required Stable Funding (RSF) factor applies to a bank's coins and banknotes and its CRR balances with RBI?

solution.explanation: Coins and banknotes immediately available to meet obligations, CRR balances (required and excess) and claims on RBI with residual maturity under six months get a zero RSF factor: they need no stable funding.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5% applies to unencumbered Level 1 assets and SLR securities; 50% and 100% apply to less liquid assets.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Available Stable Funding (ASF) in the NSFR is the portion of a bank's capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over what time horizon?

solution.explanation: RBI defines ASF as the portion of capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over the time horizon considered by the NSFR, which extends to one year. The LCR, by contrast, looks at a 30-day stress period.
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 days is the LCR horizon; three months and five years are not used.

fact_checks.claim: ASF refers to the portion of capital and liabilities expected to be reliable over the time horizon considered by the NSFR, which extends to one year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In RBI's 2025 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), HDFC Bank is placed in which bucket, and what additional CET1 requirement applies to it?

solution.explanation: RBI's list released on 2 December 2025 keeps the 2024 bucketing: SBI in bucket 4 (0.80%), HDFC Bank in bucket 2 (0.40%) and ICICI Bank in bucket 1 (0.20%). Buckets 3 and 5 are empty.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bucket 1 is ICICI Bank, bucket 4 is SBI, and bucket 3 has no bank.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank under liquidity stress, having used all its other HQLA, draws funds under the Facility to Avail Liquidity for LCR (FALLCR). On what terms is this facility available?

options.text: At 200 bps above the LAF repo rate, availed or rolled over for up to 90 days
At the Bank Rate, for up to one year
At the repo rate itself, for up to 14 days
At 100 bps above the SDF rate, for up to 30 days

solution.explanation: FALLCR is available only under stress and after all other HQLA (including MSF-eligible securities) are used, with a declaration to that effect. It can be availed or rolled over for a maximum of 90 days, the securities attract MSF haircuts, and the rate is 200 bps above the prevailing LAF repo rate.
steps: Only in stress, after exhausting other HQLA
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options give tenors and rates that RBI has not prescribed for FALLCR.
solution.final_answer: Option A: At 200 bps above the LAF repo rate, availed or rolled over for up to 90 days

fact_checks.claim: Tenor: This facility can be availed / rolled over for a maximum period of 90 days ... Facility rate: The interest rate on the funds availed under this facility shall be 200 bps above the prevailing LAF repo rate, up to a period of 90 days

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bond in a bank's stock of HQLA is downgraded and ceases to be an eligible liquid asset. Under RBI's LCR rules, what may the bank do?

options.text: Keep it in the stock of HQLA for an additional 30 calendar days to adjust or replace it
Keep it for 90 days with RBI's prior approval
Remove it from the stock on the same day
Keep it in the stock until it matures

solution.concept: Grace period after loss of eligibility
solution.explanation: RBI allows a bank to keep an asset that becomes ineligible (for example, after a downgrade) in its stock of liquid assets for an additional 30 calendar days, so that it has time to adjust its stock or replace the asset.
steps: Asset becomes ineligible → 30 more calendar days in the stock
solution.why_others_wrong: There is neither an immediate removal rule nor a 90-day or till-maturity allowance.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Keep it in the stock of HQLA for an additional 30 calendar days to adjust or replace it

fact_checks.claim: If an eligible liquid asset becomes ineligible (e.g. due to downgrade), a bank will be allowed to keep the asset in its stock of liquid assets for an additional 30 calendar days

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For the NSFR, what Available Stable Funding (ASF) factor applies to 'less stable' demand deposits and term deposits of under one year placed by retail and small business customers?

solution.explanation: Stable retail and SBC deposits (non-maturity or under one year) get a 95% ASF factor and less stable ones 90%. Short-term funding from non-financial corporates gets 50%, and capital and liabilities of one year or more get 100%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 95% is for stable deposits; 50% for non-financial corporate funding under one year; 100% for capital and long-term liabilities.

fact_checks.claim: Liabilities receiving a 90 per cent ASF factor shall comprise of 'less stable' (as defined in chapter on LCR) non-maturity (demand) deposits and /or term deposits with residual maturities of less than one year, provided by retail and SBCs

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For the LCR, 'stable' retail deposits are insured deposits held in transactional or relationship accounts. When is an account treated as 'transactional'?

options.text: When the depositor has made at least one transaction in the last 30 days
When the depositor's salary or pension is credited automatically, or bills are regularly paid from it under a registered mandate
When the depositor uses a debit card on it
When the account is a current account of any business entity

solution.explanation: RBI treats an account as transactional if the depositor's salary or pension is automatically deposited into it, or bill payments are regularly withdrawn from it through a registered mandate (ECS/NACH, utilities, loan repayments). A 'relationship' exists when, for instance, the depositor also holds another deposit, a locker, demat or loan account.
solution.why_others_wrong: A single recent transaction, debit card use or being a business current account does not meet RBI's test.
solution.final_answer: Option B: When the depositor's salary or pension is credited automatically, or bills are regularly paid from it under a registered mandate

fact_checks.claim: An account is 'transactional' if (i) the depositor's salary or pension is automatically deposited into the account, or (ii) bill payments are regularly withdrawn from the account by way of a registered mandate for ECS / NACH / utilities payments / loan repayments, etc.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI requires banks to monitor the LCR in each 'significant' currency. When is a currency considered significant for this purpose?

options.text: When the bank's aggregate liabilities in that currency are 5% or more of its total liabilities
When the currency is one of the SDR basket currencies
When it forms 25% or more of the bank's HQLA
When the bank has a branch in a country using that currency

solution.explanation: To capture currency mismatches, banks monitor the LCR in each significant currency, and a currency is significant if the aggregate liabilities denominated in it amount to 5% or more of the bank's total liabilities. Foreign bank branches, which hold no foreign-currency HQLA, need not submit this statement.
steps: Liabilities in a currency ≥ 5% of total liabilities → significant currency → monitor its LCR
solution.why_others_wrong: The SDR basket, a share of HQLA or branch presence is not the test RBI uses.
solution.final_answer: Option A: When the bank's aggregate liabilities in that currency are 5% or more of its total liabilities

fact_checks.claim: A currency is considered 'significant' if the aggregate liabilities denominated in that currency amount to 5 per cent or more of the bank's total liabilities
In order to better capture potential currency mismatches, a bank shall monitor the LCR in each significant currency

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank's balance sheet (₹ crore): regulatory capital 100; stable retail deposits under one year 500; less stable retail deposits under one year 300; deposits from non-financial corporates under one year 200. Assets: cash 50; unencumbered Level 1 securities 200; retail loans maturing within one year 300; performing loans of over one year not qualifying for a 35% or lower risk weight 500; non-performing loans 20; fixed assets 30. Using RBI's ASF and RSF factors, what is its NSFR (approximately)?

solution.why_others_wrong: 157.5% treats all retail deposits as 100% ASF; 205.4% applies 50% instead of 85% to long-term loans; 100% ignores the factors altogether.

fact_checks.claim: ASF factors: regulatory capital 100 per cent; 'stable' retail and SBC deposits of less than one year 95 per cent; 'less stable' 90 per cent; funding with residual maturity of less than one year provided by non-financial corporate customers 50 per cent

RSF factors: coins and banknotes 0 per cent; unencumbered Level 1 assets 5 per cent; loans to retail customers with residual maturity of less than one year 50 per cent; other unencumbered performing loans that do not qualify for the 35 per cent or lower risk weight with residual maturities of one year or more 85 per cent; non-performing loans and fixed assets 100 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Over the next 30 days a bank expects cash outflows of ₹1,000 crore and contractual inflows of ₹900 crore. Its stock of HQLA is ₹300 crore. What is its LCR under RBI's rules?

solution.explanation: Inflows can be recognised only up to 75% of outflows: min(900, 750) = 750. Net cash outflows = 1,000 − 750 = 250. LCR = 300 ÷ 250 = 120%, above the 100% minimum. Without the cap the ratio would wrongly appear as 300 ÷ 100 = 300%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 300% ignores the 75% cap; 30% divides by gross outflows; 92% subtracts 75% of inflows instead of capping them.

fact_checks.claim: Total expected cash inflows shall be calculated ... up to an aggregate cap of 75 per cent of total expected cash outflows
LCR shall be computed as the ratio of the stock of HQLA to the Net Cash Outflows over the next 30 calendar days

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's NSFR rules, which of the following liability–ASF factor pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.text: Term deposits of one year or more that cannot be withdrawn early without a significant penalty – 100%
Funding from RBI with residual maturity of less than six months – 0%
Funding of under one year from NABARD – 50%

solution.explanation: Operational deposits (from clearing, custody and cash management relationships) get a 50% ASF factor, not 95%. Funding under one year from national development banks such as NABARD, EXIM Bank, NaBFID, NHB and SIDBI also gets 50%; funding from RBI or other central banks maturing within six months gets 0%; liabilities including term deposits with effective residual maturity of one year or more get 100%.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three pairs are exactly as RBI prescribes.

fact_checks.claim: Liabilities receiving a 50 per cent ASF factor comprise: ... (2) Operational deposits as defined in chapter on LCR. (3) Funding with residual maturity of less than one year from sovereigns, PSEs MDBs, and national development banks (NDBs), viz., EXIM Bank, NABARD, NaBFID, NHB, and SIDBI

zero per cent ASF factor ... including funding with residual maturity of less than six months from the RBI and / or other central banks and financial institutions; 100 per cent ASF: secured and unsecured borrowings and liabilities (including term deposits) with effective residual maturities of one year or more

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's 2025 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), released on 2 December 2025:
I. The additional CET1 requirement of a D-SIB applies in addition to the Capital Conservation Buffer.
II. The D-SIB framework was first issued on 22 July 2014 and updated on 28 December 2023.
III. Axis Bank was added to the list in bucket 3, with an additional CET1 requirement of 0.60%.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI said the additional CET1 requirement for D-SIBs is in addition to the Capital Conservation Buffer, and that the framework issued on 22 July 2014 was updated on 28 December 2023. The 2025 list has only three banks: SBI (bucket 4), HDFC Bank (bucket 2) and ICICI Bank (bucket 1); bucket 3 is empty.
steps: III: wrong – no bank in bucket 3, Axis Bank not a D-SIB
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement III is false, which rules out the options containing it; II is also true, so 'I only' is incomplete.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) requirement for these D-SIBs will be in addition to the Capital Conservation Buffer ... 3 - 0.60%
The Reserve Bank had issued the 'Framework for dealing with Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs)' on July 22, 2014, which was subsequently updated on December 28, 2023

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, complaints under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme were handled by the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre and how many Offices of RBI Ombudsman?

solution.explanation: The report states that complaints are handled by 24 Offices of RBI Ombudsman (ORBIOs) together with the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC) at Chandigarh.
solution.why_others_wrong: 22, 31 and 15 are not the number given in the report.

fact_checks.claim: Under RB-IOS, 2021, the complaints are presently handled by 24 Offices of RBI Ombudsman (ORBIOs) and the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, which category accounted for the largest share of complaints received at the Offices of RBI Ombudsman in 2024-25?

solution.explanation: Loans and advances formed the largest category (29.25%). The top five – loans and advances, credit cards, mobile/electronic banking, deposit accounts and ATM/debit cards – made up 86.20% of complaints.
solution.why_others_wrong: ATM/debit cards and deposit accounts were among the top five but lower; pension complaints were not the largest.

fact_checks.claim: the top five categories of complaints, consisting of complaints related to (i) loans and advances, (ii) credit cards, (iii) mobile / electronic banking, (iv) deposit accounts, and (v) ATM / Debit cards, accounted for 86.20 per cent of all complaints received by the ORBIOs. Complaints related to Loan and Advances was the highest at 29.25 per cent

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A customer files a complaint under RB-IOS, 2026 that is directed against the management and executives of his bank rather than any deficiency in a service to him. Such a complaint is:

options.text: Maintainable only through the Contact Centre
Maintainable only if the bank is a public sector bank
Maintainable if the amount involved is below ₹30 lakh

solution.explanation: Grievances against the management or executives of a regulated entity are listed among complaints that are not maintainable under RB-IOS, 2026. The Scheme addresses deficiency in service.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bank ownership and amounts are irrelevant, and complaints cannot be filed through the Contact Centre.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Not maintainable under the Scheme

fact_checks.claim: The following types of complaints are not maintainable under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2026 ... Grievances against Management or Executives of a Regulated Entity

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, RBI's Contact Centre (toll-free 14448) operates from which centres?

solution.explanation: The report says the Contact Centre, which gives information on the grievance redress mechanism, guides complainants and provides complaint status, operates from Chandigarh, Kochi and Bhubaneswar. The CRPC itself is at Chandigarh.
steps: Contact Centre locations → Chandigarh, Kochi, Bhubaneswar
solution.why_others_wrong: Chandigarh alone is incomplete; the metros and New Delhi are not named.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Chandigarh, Kochi and Bhubaneswar

fact_checks.claim: The Contact Centre, which is operating from Chandigarh, Kochi and Bhubaneswar, received 9,27,598 calls during F.Y.2024-25

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's Contact Centre in 2024-25, from RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25:
I. It received 9,27,598 calls, up from 7,19,694 in 2023-24.
II. Most calls were attended directly by Contact Centre personnel rather than through the IVRS.
III. Abandoned calls were less than 1 per cent of the total.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Calls rose to 9,27,598 from 7,19,694. Of these, 60.64% were attended through the IVRS and 38.59% directly by personnel, so statement II is wrong. Only 0.78% (7,219) were abandoned.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong; 'I only' omits the correct statement III.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The Contact Centre received 9,27,598 calls during F.Y.2024-25, as compared to 7,19,694 in F.Y.2023-24. Of these, 60.64 per cent (5,62,452) of the calls were attended through the IVRS facility, 38.59 per cent (3,57,927) of the calls were attended directly by the CC personnel and only 0.78 per cent (7,219) of calls were abandoned

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On which mobile operating systems is the retail e₹ wallet available, according to RBI's Digital Rupee FAQs?

options.text: Only on feature phones through USSD

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs state that the e₹ wallet is available and supported on both Android and iOS devices; users download the e₹ app of a participating bank or non-bank from the Play Store or App Store.
solution.why_others_wrong: It is not limited to one platform, and RBI does not describe a USSD-only wallet.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Both Android and iOS

fact_checks.claim: e₹ wallet is available and supported both on Android and iOS mobile devices

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Can a user load e₹ from a bank account into an e₹ wallet, or redeem it back, outside banking hours?

options.text: No, only during the bank's working hours
Only on working days, from 8 AM to 8 PM
Yes, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say e₹ can be loaded, redeemed or transferred between one's bank account and the e₹ wallet 24x7.
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no banking-hours or branch restriction.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Yes, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

fact_checks.claim: Yes. e₹ can be loaded / redeemed / transferred from / to one's bank account to / from the e₹ wallet 24 hours x 7 days a week

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A user has a dispute about an e₹ (digital rupee) transaction. According to RBI's Digital Rupee FAQs, how can she raise it?

options.text: Only by writing to the Department of Currency Management
Through her e₹ wallet app or by contacting the wallet provider's customer care
Only by filing a complaint at an RBI regional office
Only through the RBI Ombudsman directly

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say users can raise disputes via their e₹ wallet app or reach out to their customer care centre, i.e. with the bank or non-bank providing the wallet.
steps: e₹ dispute → wallet app or provider's customer care
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI does not require users to go first to its offices, the Ombudsman or a central department.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Through her e₹ wallet app or by contacting the wallet provider's customer care

fact_checks.claim: Users can raise disputes via their e₹ wallet app or reach out to their customer care centre

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Authentication Directions, 2025, if a customer suffers a loss from a digital payment effected without complying with these Directions, who bears it?

options.text: The customer, unless he reports it within three days
The merchant who accepted the payment
The payment system operator such as NPCI
The issuer, which must compensate the customer in full without demur

solution.explanation: The Directions state that if any loss arises out of transactions effected without complying with them, the issuer shall compensate the customer for the loss in full without demur.
steps: Non-compliant authentication + loss → issuer compensates fully
solution.why_others_wrong: The rule places the loss on the issuer, not on the customer, network operator or merchant.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The issuer, which must compensate the customer in full without demur

fact_checks.claim: If any loss arises out of transactions effected without complying with these directions, the issuer shall compensate the customer for the loss in full without demur

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026 require banks to provide which facility on their mobile and internet banking applications?

options.text: A facility to switch off all authentication for small payments
A mechanism for customers, with authentication, to mark a transaction as fraudulent for immediate notification to the bank
An option for customers to reverse any transaction themselves within 24 hours
A chat facility with RBI's Ombudsman

solution.concept: Customer fraud reporting in digital channels
solution.explanation: Banks must let customers, with necessary authentication, identify or mark a transaction as fraudulent in the app or internet banking for seamless and immediate notification, and should build capability to report it instantly to the beneficiary's bank.
steps: In-app 'mark as fraud' → immediate notice to bank → onward reporting to beneficiary entity
solution.why_others_wrong: Self-reversal, switching off authentication and an Ombudsman chat are not required.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A mechanism for customers, with authentication, to mark a transaction as fraudulent for immediate notification to the bank

fact_checks.claim: The bank shall provide a mechanism on its mobile and internet banking application for its customers, with necessary authentication, to identify / mark a transaction as fraudulent for seamless and immediate notification to the bank

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Bank P received RBI's approval for mobile banking in 2024, before the Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025 took effect. Bank Q received approval for a transactional facility under these Directions in March 2026. Both now wish to launch internet banking. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both must apply afresh to RBI for prior approval of internet banking
Both may launch it without any further step, since each already has an approval
P may launch it freely, but Q must seek fresh approval because its approval was channel-specific

Q may launch it under its existing approval; P must first ensure it meets the eligibility criteria (CBS/IPv6, CRAR, capital, financial and technical capability) and send a GAICA report for the new channel within 30 days of its decision

solution.concept: Scope of approval for digital channels
solution.explanation: Once approval is granted under the 2025 Directions, a bank can provide all types of digital banking channels, so Q needs nothing more. A bank approved for a particular channel before the Directions applied must ensure compliance with criteria 7.1(a) to (d) before launching any other channel and send the GAICA report (certified by CERT-In empanelled auditors) for the new channel to RBI's Department of Regulation through PRAVAAH within thirty days of the decision to launch.
steps: Approval under the 2025 Directions → all channels (Q)
Pre-2026 channel-specific approval → meet 7.1(a)–(d) + GAICA report within 30 days (P)
solution.why_others_wrong: Neither bank needs a fresh prior approval; P cannot launch without meeting the criteria; Q's approval is not channel-specific.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Q may launch it under its existing approval; P must first ensure it meets the eligibility criteria (CBS/IPv6, CRAR, capital, financial and technical capability) and send a GAICA report for the new channel within 30 days of its decision

fact_checks.claim: Once an approval is granted under these Directions, the bank can provide all types of digital banking channels. If a bank had received approval for a particular digital banking channel (like mobile banking) before the date of applicability of these Directions, it shall ensure compliance to the eligibility criteria as detailed in para 7.1(a) to (d) above before launching any other digital banking channel. Further, the GAICA Report ... shall be sent to the Department of Regulation ... within thirty days from the decision to launch the facility

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about cross-border card transactions under RBI's Authentication Directions, 2025:
I. The two-factor and other principles of the Directions apply in full to all cross-border digital payments.
II. By 1 October 2026, card issuers had to put in place a mechanism to validate non-recurring cross-border card-not-present transactions where authentication is requested by an overseas merchant or acquirer.
III. For this purpose, card issuers must register their Bank Identification Numbers (BINs) with the card networks.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Directions apply to domestic digital payments and are not applicable to cross-border transactions. However, card issuers had to set up, by 1 October 2026, a mechanism to validate non-recurring cross-border card-not-present transactions where the overseas merchant or acquirer raises an authentication request, register their BINs with card networks, and adopt a risk-based mechanism for all cross-border CNP transactions.
steps: I: wrong – the Directions cover domestic transactions
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I is false, which rules out options containing it; 'III only' omits the correct statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: II and III only

fact_checks.claim: The directions outlined above are not applicable to cross-border digital payment transactions. However, card issuers shall, by October 01, 2026, put in place a mechanism to validate non-recurring, cross-border card not present (CNP) transactions, where request for authentication is raised by an overseas merchant or overseas acquirer. To ensure compliance, card issuers shall register their Bank Identification Numbers (BINs) with card networks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
A bank allows its customers to register the mobile banking app on more than one device. Under RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026, which of the following must it do?
I. Bind the app to the device using a combination of hardware, software and service information.
II. Notify the user of every new device registration on multiple channels, such as the registered mobile number, e-mail or a phone call.
III. Keep a record of all registered devices and give the user a facility to disable a registered device.
IV. Limit the user to a maximum of two registered devices.

solution.explanation: Banks must ensure device binding through a combination of hardware, software and service information. Where multiple devices are allowed, the user must be notified of every new device registration on multiple channels, and the bank must keep a record of all registered devices with a facility for the user to disable any of them. No numerical cap on devices is prescribed.
steps: IV → no such cap in the Directions
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with IV add a cap RBI has not set; 'I and II only' leaves out the device-record requirement.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I, II and III only

fact_checks.claim: The bank shall ensure device binding of the mobile application. Device binding shall be implemented through a combination of hardware, software, and service information. In case, the bank allows multiple devices to be registered, then, (i) the user shall be notified of every new device registration on multiple channels such as registered mobile number, email, or phone call, and (ii) in relation to the mobile application, the bank shall maintain a record of all registered devices, providing the user a facility to disable a registered device

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026 make some mobile-app controls mandatory ('shall') and leave others to the bank's discretion ('may'). Which of the following are mandatory?
I. Hosting the checksum of the current active version of the app on a public platform.
II. Checking whether the phone is rooted or jailbroken before the app is installed.
III. Not storing user IDs, passwords or keys on the device.
IV. Implementing alternatives to SMS-based OTP.

solution.explanation: Banks shall host the checksum of the current active app version publicly, and the app shall not store sensitive authentication information such as user IDs, passwords, keys or hashes on the device. By contrast, a bank 'may explore' a rooted/jailbroken-device check and 'may implement' alternatives to SMS-based OTP.
steps: No storing credentials on device → shall
solution.why_others_wrong: II and IV are optional; 'III only' misses the mandatory checksum.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The bank shall host the checksum of current active version of its mobile application on public platform so that users can verify the same

The bank may explore the feasibility of implementing a code that checks if the device is rooted / jailbroken prior to the installation of the mobile application ... The bank may implement alternatives to SMS-based OTP authentication mechanisms ... The mobile application shall not store / retain sensitive personal / customer authentication information such as user IDs, passwords, keys, hashes

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the principles in RBI's Authentication Directions, 2025:
I. For every digital payment, including card-present transactions, at least one authentication factor must be dynamically created or proven.
II. Issuers may apply checks beyond the minimum two factors based on behavioural or contextual parameters such as location, device attributes and transaction history.
III. Issuers may, at their discretion, offer customers a choice of authentication factors.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The dynamic-factor rule applies to digital payments other than card-present transactions, so statement I is wrong. Issuers may use risk-based checks on behavioural and contextual parameters beyond the two-factor minimum (and may explore DigiLocker for high-risk transactions), and may offer customers a choice of factors.
steps: I: wrong – card-present transactions are outside the dynamic-factor rule
solution.why_others_wrong: Every option containing statement I is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: II and III only

fact_checks.claim: It shall be ensured that for digital payment transactions, other than card present transactions, at least one of the factors of authentication is dynamically created or proven

Issuers may, in line with their internal risk management policies, identify transactions for evaluation against behavioural / contextual parameters ... additional checks beyond the minimum two-factor authentication may be resorted to; Issuers may, at their discretion, offer a choice of authentication factors to their customers

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility Scheme, if the beneficiary does not have an account with Nepal SBI Ltd or lives in an area not served by its branches, cash in Nepalese rupees is delivered through:

Otherwise → cash through Prabhu Money Transfer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In August 2021, RBI enhanced the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility Scheme. According to RBI's FAQs, the enhancement was meant to:

options.text: Allow remittances from Nepal to India through NEFT for the first time
Boost trade payments between India and Nepal and facilitate retirement and pension payments to ex-servicemen settled in Nepal
Shift the scheme from NEFT to UPI for all remittances
Let Nepalese banks become direct members of India's NEFT system

It remains one-way, from India to Nepal.

solution.final_answer: Option B: Boost trade payments between India and Nepal and facilitate retirement and pension payments to ex-servicemen settled in Nepal

a cross-border remittance scheme to transfer funds from India to Nepal (one-way only), enabled under the NEFT ecosystem

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A company sends ₹60 crore by NEFT to a supplier company, but the remitting bank's message does not carry the beneficiary's Legal Entity Identifier (LEI). According to RBI's FAQs on LEI, how should the beneficiary bank treat this inward transaction?

options.text: It must reject the transaction and return it to the remitting bank within two hours
It must hold the credit until the remitter furnishes the LEI
It should not reject the transaction; both banks must maintain valid, verified LEI information after credit
It may credit the amount only if the beneficiary is an individual

solution.explanation: All single NEFT/RTGS payments of ₹50 crore and above by non-individuals must carry remitter and beneficiary LEI, and the remitting bank should ensure both are captured. But an inward transaction with inappropriate or no LEI should not be rejected by the beneficiary bank; after credit, both banks should maintain valid and verified LEI information.
steps: Missing LEI on inward → do not reject
Post-credit → both banks maintain valid LEI
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI says such transactions should not be rejected or held; a company-to-company payment is not an individual transaction.
solution.final_answer: Option C: It should not reject the transaction; both banks must maintain valid, verified LEI information after credit

fact_checks.claim: Any inward transaction with inappropriate or no LEI should not be rejected by beneficiary bank. However, post-credit, both remitting and beneficiary banks should maintain valid and verified LEI information for all payment transactions of ₹50 crore and above

All single payment transactions of ₹50 crore and above undertaken by entities (non-individuals) should include remitter and beneficiary LEI information. This is applicable to transactions undertaken through the NEFT and RTGS payment systems

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's FAQs on the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) for large value transactions:
I. The LEI is a 20-character alpha-numeric code, obtainable in India from Legal Entity Identifier India Ltd.
II. In NEFT messages, the first two lines of the optional field 7495 are used to capture the sender's and the beneficiary's LEI, in that order.
III. In RTGS, the LEI requirement for payments of ₹50 crore and above applies to customer payments but not to inter-bank transactions.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The LEI is a 20-character code issued by LOUs accredited by GLEIF; in India, by LEIL (I correct). In NEFT the first two lines of field 7495 carry sender and beneficiary LEI, with narration in the last four lines (II correct). In RTGS both customer payments and inter-bank transactions of ₹50 crore and above must carry LEI (III wrong).
steps: III: RTGS inter-bank also covered → wrong
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option including III is wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is a 20-character alpha-numeric code ... In India, LEI can be obtained from Legal Entity Identifier India Ltd.
In NEFT payment messages, the field 7495 ... The first two lines of this field hall be used for capturing sender and beneficiary customer LEI information, in that order
In case of RTGS, both customer payment and inter-bank transactions meeting the above criterion should include LEI information

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT among the details a remitting customer must furnish to the bank for an RTGS remittance, according to RBI's RTGS FAQs?

options.text: The account number to be debited
The IFSC of the receiving branch

solution.explanation: The FAQs list: the account to be debited, the beneficiary bank and branch, the IFSC of the receiving branch, the beneficiary's name and account number, any sender-to-receiver information, and the sender and beneficiary LEI for eligible transactions. The beneficiary's PAN is not required.
steps: Required: debit account, beneficiary bank/branch, IFSC, beneficiary name and account, LEI if eligible
solution.why_others_wrong: IFSC, beneficiary account number and debit account are all on RBI's list.

fact_checks.claim: The account number to be debited; Name of the beneficiary bank and branch; The IFSC number of the receiving branch; Name of the beneficiary customer; Account number of the beneficiary customer; Sender to receiver information, if any; Sender and Beneficiary Legal Entity Identifier (for eligible transactions)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's RTGS FAQs, where are the timelines for processing applications for the services of RBI's Department of Payment and Settlement Systems under the PSS Act, 2007 published?

options.text: In the RTGS System Regulations only
They are not published; each application is decided case by case

solution.concept: Service timelines under the PSS Act
solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say RBI has published a Citizens' Charter defining timelines for services offered by its departments, including those of the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems under the PSS Act, 2007. The membership procedure itself is in the RTGS System Regulations.
solution.why_others_wrong: The RTGS Regulations give the procedure, not the departmental service timelines; NPCI has no role here.
solution.final_answer: Option A: In RBI's Citizens' Charter

fact_checks.claim: RBI has published Citizens' Charter, wherein, timelines are defined for various services offered by the respective departments. The timelines for the services offered by the Department of Payment and Settlement Systems under the PSS Act, 2007 are available

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the LEI requirement in RTGS, based on RBI's FAQs:
I. It applies to all channels used to connect to RTGS, including thick-client, Web-API and the Payment Originator module.
II. Ministries and Departments of the Central Government must quote their LEI for RTGS payments of ₹50 crore and above.
III. In RTGS messages, the sender's and beneficiary's LEIs are captured in the first two loops of the relevant optional field.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The LEI instructions apply to all RTGS channels: thick-client, Web-API (through INFINET or another approved network) and the Payment Originator module (I correct). Governments and their Departments/Ministries need not obtain or quote LEI, though Government corporations must (II wrong). In RTGS messages the first two loops carry sender and beneficiary LEI, and narration goes in the last two (III correct).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong; 'I only' misses III.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The LEI instructions are applicable to all the channels being used for connecting to RTGS viz. thick-client, Web-API (through INFINET or any other approved network) and Payment Originator (PO) module
It is not necessary for Governments or their Departments / Ministries to obtain LEI or mention LEI number for payment transactions in NEFT and RTGS
The first two loops of this field shall be used for capturing sender and beneficiary customer LEI information, in that order

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's turn-around time (TAT) framework for failed transactions in authorised payment systems such as IMPS, how is the compensation for delay paid to the customer?

options.text: Only after the RBI Ombudsman passes an award
It is credited to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim
By NPCI directly, in cash at the bank branch
Only after the customer files a complaint with the bank

solution.explanation: RBI's circular of 20 September 2019 says that wherever financial compensation is involved, it must be credited to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim. Customers who do not get redress within the TAT can complain under RBI's Integrated Ombudsman Scheme.
solution.why_others_wrong: No complaint, Ombudsman award or cash payment by NPCI is required.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It is credited to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim

fact_checks.claim: Wherever financial compensation is involved, the same shall be effected to the customer's account suo moto, without waiting for a complaint or claim from the customer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which transactions are covered by RBI's harmonised turn-around time (TAT) and compensation framework for failed transactions in authorised payment systems such as IMPS and UPI?

options.text: All transactions of Indian customers, including remittances abroad
Domestic transactions, where both the originator and the beneficiary are within India
Only transactions through bank branches, not through mobile apps

solution.explanation: The framework's general instructions say it covers domestic transactions, i.e., those where both the originator and the beneficiary are within India. It applies across authorised payment systems and to non-banks wherever they are authorised to operate, with no amount threshold or channel restriction.
solution.why_others_wrong: Cross-border transactions are excluded; there is no amount threshold or channel restriction.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Domestic transactions, where both the originator and the beneficiary are within India

fact_checks.claim: Domestic transactions i.e., those where both the originator and beneficiary are within India are covered under this framework

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
RBI's TAT framework for failed transactions states two principles. Apply them to these IMPS cases:
Case 1: Asha's account is debited for a credit-push transfer, but Bina's account is not credited within the prescribed time.
Case 2: Chetan's bank delays initiating his transfer beyond the TAT.
To whom is the penalty payable in each case?

options.text: Case 1: to Asha (the originator); Case 2: to Chetan (the originator)
Case 1: to Bina; Case 2: to Chetan's intended beneficiary
Case 1: to Bina (the beneficiary); Case 2: to Chetan (the originator)
In both cases the penalty is paid to NPCI's customer protection fund

solution.explanation: The framework says: if a credit-push transfer is debited to the originator but the beneficiary account is not credited, credit must be given within the prescribed time, failing which the penalty is paid to the beneficiary; if there is delay in initiating the transaction at the originator bank's end beyond the TAT, the penalty is paid to the originator.
steps: Delay in credit to beneficiary → penalty to beneficiary (Bina)
Delay in initiation at originator's bank → penalty to originator (Chetan)
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options misplace the recipient of the penalty; there is no NPCI fund in the framework.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Case 1: to Bina (the beneficiary); Case 2: to Chetan (the originator)

fact_checks.claim: If the transaction is a 'credit-push' funds transfer and the beneficiary account is not credited while the debit to originator has been effected, then credit is to be effected within the prescribed time period failing which the penalty has to be paid to the beneficiary; If there is delay in initiation of a transaction at the originator bank's end beyond the TAT, then penalty has to be paid to the originator

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Authentication Directions, 2025 require at least two factors of authentication for digital payments, with listed exemptions. Which UPI use case was added to the list of exemptions through a letter to NPCI in September 2026?

options.text: UPI payments above ₹1 lakh to hospitals
Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled point-of-sale machines
UPI person-to-person transfers to new payees

solution.explanation: Annexure-1 of the Reserve Bank of India (Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions) Directions, 2025 lists the exemptions in force, such as small-value contactless card payments, recurring e-mandate debits (other than the first), NETC transactions and small-value offline payments. It now includes Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled PoS machines, under a letter to NPCI dated 2 September 2026.
steps: Tap and Pay UPI on NFC PoS → letter of 2 September 2026
solution.why_others_wrong: The other UPI uses are not in the exemption list.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Tap and Pay UPI payments on NFC-enabled point-of-sale machines

fact_checks.claim: Tap and Pay UPI Payment on Near Field Communication enabled Point of Sale machines Letter dated September 2, 2026 (CO.DPSS.POLC.No. S-550/02-23-001/2026-27 dated September 2, 2026) issued to NPCI

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, which also governs UPI AutoPay, what must the issuer's post-transaction notification include at the minimum, besides the merchant's name, amount, date and time and reference numbers?

options.text: A one-time password to confirm the debit
The customer's credit score and available balance
The reason for the debit (the e-mandate registered by the customer) and details on grievance redressal

solution.explanation: After an e-mandate debit, the issuer must send a post-transaction notification giving at least the merchant's name, transaction amount, date and time, reference numbers of the transaction and e-mandate, the reason for the debit (the customer's registered e-mandate) and details on grievance redressal, the last added on the basis of feedback.
steps: Post-debit notice: merchant, amount, date/time, references, reason, grievance redressal details
solution.why_others_wrong: Credit score, merchant tax IDs or an OTP are not required; recurring debits after the first need no AFA within limits.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The reason for the debit (the e-mandate registered by the customer) and details on grievance redressal

fact_checks.claim: An issuer shall send a post-transaction notification to the customer. This notification shall, at the minimum, inform the customer about the merchant's name, transaction amount, date and time of debit, reference number of transaction and e-mandate, reason for debit, i.e., e-mandate registered by the customer, and details on grievance redressal

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, a customer wants to change the validity period of her UPI AutoPay mandate. What does the framework require for any modification or withdrawal of an existing e-mandate?

options.text: A written request at the home branch
Nothing; it can be changed by the merchant on the customer's request

solution.explanation: The issuer must let the customer modify the validity period or withdraw the e-mandate at any time, and any modification in, or withdrawal of, an existing e-mandate requires AFA validation by the issuer.
steps: Validated with AFA by the issuer
solution.why_others_wrong: No branch visit or merchant approval is needed, and the merchant cannot alter it.
solution.final_answer: Option D: AFA validation by the issuer

fact_checks.claim: Any modification in, or withdrawal of, an existing e-mandate shall require AFA validation by the issuer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: From 1 August 2025, NPCI moved the execution of UPI AutoPay mandate debits to non-peak hours. Which periods does NPCI define as peak hours?

options.text: 9 am to 12 noon and 4 pm to 8 pm
10 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 9:30 pm
8 am to 11 am and 6 pm to 10 pm
12 noon to 3 pm and 7 pm to 11 pm

solution.explanation: NPCI's May 2025 circular defines peak hours as 10:00 to 13:00 and 17:00 to 21:30, when UPI transactions reach their highest transactions per second; any other time is non-peak. AutoPay mandates can still be created at any time, but their execution is moved to non-peak hours.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other windows are not those NPCI specified.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 10 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 9:30 pm

fact_checks.claim: Peak hours are defined as the period during the day when UPI financial transactions reach the highest transactions per second, observed from 10:00 hrs (10 am) to 13:00 hrs (1 pm) and from 17:00 hrs (5 pm) to 21:30 hrs (9.30 pm)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Master Direction on Prepaid Payment Instruments, how is interoperability across PPIs issued in the form of wallets to be enabled?

options.text: Through the Bharat Bill Payment System
Through the RuPay card network only

solution.explanation: The PPI Master Direction says that where PPIs are issued as wallets, interoperability across PPIs shall be enabled through UPI; PPIs in the form of cards achieve interoperability through authorised card networks. Since *99# USSD is part of UPI, non-bank PPI issuers may also participate in it.
solution.why_others_wrong: Card networks serve card PPIs; NEFT and BBPS are not the interoperability route for wallets.

fact_checks.claim: Where PPIs are issued in the form of wallets, interoperability across PPIs shall be enabled through UPI
Since *99# USSD is part of UPI, non-bank PPI issuer are also allowed to participate in the same

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about UPI payments from PPIs under RBI's Master Direction on PPIs:
I. A UPI payment from a PPI made on the issuer's own application is authenticated using the customer's existing PPI credentials.
II. If the PPI is linked to a third-party UPI application, the payment is authenticated using UPI credentials.
III. A PPI issuer acting as a PSP may onboard customers of any bank onto its UPI handle.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: On the issuer's own app, UPI transactions from a PPI use the existing PPI credentials and are thus pre-approved before reaching UPI (I correct). A full-KYC PPI discovered on a third-party UPI app is authenticated with UPI credentials (II correct). A PPI issuer, as PSP, shall not onboard customers of any bank or other PPI issuer (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: UPI transactions from PPI on the issuer's application shall be authenticated using the customer's existing PPI credentials ... A PPI issuer, in its capacity as a PSP, shall not on-board customers of any bank or any other PPI issuer
Such UPI transactions, from PPIs using third party UPI applications, shall be authenticated using the UPI credentials

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Neha's UPI Lite balance is ₹1,700. Under RBI's current limits for UPI Lite, (a) what is the most she can add right now, and (b) after topping up fully, what is the minimum number of UPI Lite payments needed to pay ₹4,600 to a merchant entirely from UPI Lite?

solution.explanation: The UPI Lite balance cannot exceed ₹5,000 at any time, so she can add at most ₹5,000 − ₹1,700 = ₹3,300 (online, with AFA). Each UPI Lite payment is capped at ₹1,000, so ₹4,600 needs at least ⌈4,600 ÷ 1,000⌉ = 5 payments.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 payments can carry at most ₹4,000; ₹5,000 ignores the existing balance; ₹300 and 10 use the general offline limits of ₹2,000 and ₹500.

fact_checks.claim: For UPI Lite, the enhanced limits shall be ₹1,000 per transaction with ₹5,000 being the total limit. Replenishment of used limit shall be allowed only in online mode with AFA

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Bharat Bill Payment System Directions, 2024, what must happen before a bill payment is initiated through BBPS (other than for prepaid services)?

options.text: The biller must send a paper bill to the customer
The customer must visit an agent outlet

solution.explanation: The Directions describe BBPS, operated by NPCI's subsidiary NBBL, as an integrated platform for paying bills through multiple channels and modes; transactions require the bill to be fetched before payment initiation, while for prepaid services the customer's relationship with the biller is validated through the platform.
solution.why_others_wrong: Paper bills, agent visits or NPCI approval of each payment are not required.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The bill must be fetched

fact_checks.claim: The transactions facilitated through this platform will require the bill to be fetched before payment initiation. In case of transactions involving payments for prepaid services, the customer relationship with the biller will be validated through the platform

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, for which of the following e-mandates is the issuer NOT required to send a pre-transaction notification before the debit?

options.text: E-mandates for credit card bill payments
E-mandates registered to auto-replenish FASTag and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) balances

solution.explanation: Issuers must normally send a pre-transaction notification at least 24 hours before an e-mandate debit, but it is not required for e-mandates registered to auto-replenish FASTag and NCMC balances.
solution.why_others_wrong: SIPs, insurance premiums and credit card bills have a higher AFA-free limit but still need pre-debit notices.
solution.final_answer: Option B: E-mandates registered to auto-replenish FASTag and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC) balances

fact_checks.claim: Pre-transaction notification is not required for e-mandates registered to auto-replenish balances of FASTag, and National Common Mobility Card (NCMC)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025) describe the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS)?

options.text: A card-based system in which customers use RuPay debit cards at ATMs
A bank-led model for interoperable financial inclusion transactions at micro-ATM terminals through Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication
A system for bulk credit of salaries operated by UIDAI
A non-bank wallet system regulated as a prepaid payment instrument

solution.explanation: RBI describes AePS as a bank-led model that facilitates online interoperable financial inclusion transactions at PoS (micro-ATM) terminals through banks' Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication; UIDAI verifies biometrics and NPCI handles switching, clearing and settlement.
steps: AePS: bank-led, BC micro-ATMs, Aadhaar authentication
solution.why_others_wrong: AePS is not card-based or a wallet system, and UIDAI does not operate a bulk-credit system.
solution.final_answer: Option B: A bank-led model for interoperable financial inclusion transactions at micro-ATM terminals through Business Correspondents, using Aadhaar authentication

fact_checks.claim: Aadhaar-enabled Payment System (AePS) is a bank-led model that facilitates online interoperable financial inclusion transactions at Point of Sale (Micro ATM) terminals through Business Correspondents of banks, using Aadhaar authentication

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's framework on turn-around time for failed transactions, there is a delay in crediting a beneficiary's account through the Aadhaar Payments Bridge System (APBS), used for government benefits. What must be done?

options.text: NPCI must credit the beneficiary from its own funds within T + 3 days
No time limit applies, as APBS payments are government transfers
The remitting government department must re-send the payment within T + 5 days
The beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day, with ₹100 per day of delay beyond that

solution.explanation: For APBS, where there is a delay in crediting the beneficiary's account, the beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day; compensation of ₹100 per day applies if the delay goes beyond T + 1.
steps: APBS credit delay → beneficiary bank reverses by T + 1
solution.why_others_wrong: The framework places the duty on the beneficiary bank, not the department or NPCI, and APBS is covered.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The beneficiary bank must reverse the transaction within T + 1 day, with ₹100 per day of delay beyond that

fact_checks.claim: Aadhaar Payment Bridge System (APBS) a Delay in crediting beneficiary's account. Beneficiary bank to reverse the transaction within T + 1 day. ₹100/- per day if delay is beyond T + 1 day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Bharat Bill Payment System (BBPS) under RBI's BBPS Directions, 2024, operated by NPCI's subsidiary NPCI Bharat BillPay Ltd (NBBL):
I. A non-bank BBPOU must open an escrow account with a scheduled commercial bank exclusively for BBPS transactions.
II. A sponsor bank, which is a scheduled commercial bank, facilitates settlement of non-bank BBPOUs with NBBL.
III. A Customer Operating Unit (COU) is the entity that onboards billers onto the BBPS platform.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Non-bank BBPOUs must keep an escrow account with an SCB exclusively for BBPS (I correct). A sponsor bank (an SCB) facilitates their settlement with NBBL (II correct). Billers are onboarded by a Biller Operating Unit (BOU); a COU provides customers the interface to pay bills (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III confuse COU and BOU; 'II only' misses I.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: A non-bank BBPOU shall open an escrow account with a Scheduled Commercial Bank exclusively for BBPS transactions
Sponsor bank: A Scheduled Commercial Bank which facilitates settlement of non-bank BBPOUs with NBBL
Biller Operating Unit (BOU) is an entity which onboards biller(s) ... Customer Operating Unit (COU) is an entity which provides its customers with an interface (physical / digital) to pay bills

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which kinds of deposits may a payments bank accept under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025?

options.text: Only fixed deposits of up to one year
Savings, current and fixed deposits up to ₹2 lakh
Only demand deposits, i.e. current and savings deposits

solution.explanation: Payments banks may undertake only restricted activities such as accepting demand deposits — current and savings bank deposits. They cannot accept term deposits, and the ₹2 lakh end-of-day cap per individual applies.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fixed and recurring deposits are term deposits, which payments banks cannot accept.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Only demand deposits, i.e. current and savings deposits

fact_checks.claim: PBs may undertake only certain restricted activities such as acceptance of demand deposits, i.e., current deposits, and savings bank deposits

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A payments bank offers 'view only' mobile banking. Which service can it provide through it?

options.text: Balance enquiry and account statement download
Applying for and receiving a loan

solution.explanation: A view-only facility offers only services that do not alter the customer's assets or liabilities, such as balance enquiry, balance viewing and statement download. Fund transfers and other facilities that move funds or create liability need a transactional facility.
steps: View only = no change in assets/liabilities
solution.why_others_wrong: Fund transfers, loans and bill payments move funds or create liabilities.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Balance enquiry and account statement download

fact_checks.claim: View Only Banking Facility – A feature of digital banking channels which only allows banking services that do not alter the asset or liability of the customer viz. balance enquiry, balance viewing, account statement download, etc. ... Loans, funds transfers, and other such facilities ... cannot be provided by banks having view only facility

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT among the eligibility criteria for a payments bank to get RBI's approval for a transactional internet/mobile banking facility?

options.text: A minimum of five years of profitable operations
Core Banking Solution and IPv6-enabled public-facing IT infrastructure
Compliance with the minimum regulatory CRAR
A GAICA report certified by a CERT-In empanelled auditor

solution.explanation: The criteria include CBS and IPv6 readiness, compliance with minimum CRAR, minimum capital/net worth as per licensing norms, adequate financial and technical capability, and a satisfactory compliance record shown by a GAICA report certified by CERT-In empanelled auditors. A five-year profit record is not a criterion.
steps: CBS + IPv6; CRAR; net worth; capability; GAICA (CERT-In auditor)
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are listed criteria.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A minimum of five years of profitable operations

fact_checks.claim: Implementation of CBS and public facing IT infrastructure being enabled to handle IPv6 traffic. Compliance with minimum regulatory CRAR requirement. Minimum paid up capital/Net worth as per the applicable licensing requirement ... A GAICA Report ... certified by (third party) CERT-In empaneled auditor(s)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A company has fund-based and non-fund-based facilities of ₹12 crore from the banking system and wants a current account with a payments bank. Under the current account rules in RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025 (as updated), what can the payments bank offer?

options.text: A normal current account without restriction
Only a collection account, whose credits must be remitted within two working days to the designated cash credit, overdraft or current account
A current account, provided the balance stays below ₹2 lakh
Nothing, as payments banks cannot open current accounts

solution.explanation: A bank may maintain a current account without restriction only where the banking system's aggregate exposure to the customer is below ₹10 crore. At ₹10 crore or more, only a collection account is allowed; funds credited must be remitted within two working days to the designated CC/OD/current account (after statutory dues and dues to the bank). ₹12 crore ≥ ₹10 crore, so only a collection account.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹12 crore exceeds the threshold; payments banks can open current accounts; the ₹2 lakh cap concerns individuals.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Only a collection account, whose credits must be remitted within two working days to the designated cash credit, overdraft or current account

fact_checks.claim: A bank may maintain current account without any restriction in case of customers where the aggregate exposure of the banking system to the customer is less than ₹10 crore ... A bank may maintain only collection accounts in case of customers to whom the exposure of the banking system is ₹10 crore or more

Funds credited into a collection account shall be remitted within two working days of receipt of such funds to a Cash Credit Account (CC), current account, or Overdraft Account (OD) ... designated by the borrower

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 10 November 2026 a payments bank finds that the banking system's exposure to a customer holding an ordinary current account with it has risen to ₹10.5 crore. Under RBI's Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025, what must it do?

options.text: Close the account the same day
Nothing until the next half-yearly review
Convert the account into a savings account within a week
Notify the customer by 10 December 2026 that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete this by 10 February 2027

solution.explanation: Banks must monitor accounts at least once every half-year. When a customer becomes ineligible because exposure has reached ₹10 crore, the bank must notify the customer promptly and within one month that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete the conversion or closure within three months of observing the ineligibility.
solution.why_others_wrong: Immediate closure is not required; waiting for the review or converting to savings is not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Notify the customer by 10 December 2026 that the account must be converted to a collection account or closed, and complete this by 10 February 2027

fact_checks.claim: the bank shall notify the customer(s) concerned promptly, and in any case within one month from the date of observing such ineligibility, that the account must either be converted to a collection account or closed. The conversion or closure process ... shall be completed within three months of observing such ineligibility
all banks shall monitor accounts maintained with them on a regular basis, and in any case at least once every half-year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the SFB Licensing Guidelines, 2025, proposals from which of the following will NOT be entertained for setting up a small finance bank?

options.text: Resident professionals with 10 years' senior experience in banking and finance
Resident-controlled microfinance institutions with a five-year track record
Resident-controlled NBFCs with a five-year track record

solution.explanation: Proposals from AIFs will not be entertained, nor from government-owned entities, large industrial houses, state financial corporations and some others. Resident professionals, NBFCs and MFIs meeting the criteria are eligible.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are eligible categories.

fact_checks.claim: The proposals from Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) will also not be entertained

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which statement on voting rights and share acquisition applies to small finance banks under the SFB Licensing Guidelines, 2025?

options.text: Acquisition of up to 25% needs no approval
There is no cap on voting rights for SFBs
Voting rights are capped at 10%, and acquiring 1% needs RBI's approval
A shareholder's voting rights are capped at 26%, and acquiring 5% or more needs RBI's prior approval

solution.concept: Voting rights in private banks and SFBs
solution.explanation: Under Section 12(2) of the BR Act read with RBI's 2016 notification, any shareholder's voting rights in a private sector bank are capped at 26%, and under Section 12B acquiring 5% or more of paid-up capital or voting rights needs RBI's prior approval. Both apply to SFBs.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other caps and thresholds are not those in the BR Act.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: Triparty repo made up about 72.5% of the overnight volume, while call money made up under 2%
Call money was the largest segment, at about 72.5% of the overnight volume
Market repo made up about half of the overnight volume
The segment with the highest rate also had the highest volume

solution.concept: Composition of the overnight money market
solution.explanation: Total overnight volume = 14,431.90 + 5,72,289.15 + 1,95,543.41 + 7,492.65 = ₹7,89,757.11 crore. Triparty repo is 5,72,289.15 ÷ 7,89,757.11 ≈ 72.5%; call money is about 1.8%; market repo about 24.8%. The highest rate (5.71%, corporate bond repo) belongs to the smallest segment.
solution.why_others_wrong: Call money is the smallest overnight segment; market repo is about a quarter, not half; corporate bond repo has the highest rate but the smallest volume.
