The cut-off yields were 5.8970% and 6.6485%. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The 91-day bill had the higher bid-cover ratio (about 2.70 against 2.56)
The 364-day bill had the higher bid-cover ratio (about 2.70 against 2.56) and the higher cut-off yield
Both bills had the same bid-cover ratio of about 2.6
The 364-day bill had the lower cut-off yield, as it was more heavily bid

solution.explanation: Bid-cover ratio = competitive bids received ÷ notified amount. 91-day: 20,465.33 ÷ 8,000 ≈ 2.56. 364-day: 18,875 ÷ 7,000 ≈ 2.70. The 364-day cut-off yield (6.6485%) was also higher than the 91-day yield (5.8970%), as is usual for the longer tenor.
solution.why_others_wrong: The ratios are swapped in the second option and not equal; the 364-day yield was higher, not lower.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The 364-day bill had the higher bid-cover ratio (about 2.70 against 2.56) and the higher cut-off yield

questions.question_text: What did the IRDAI (Insurance Intermediaries) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026 change for corporate agents?

options.text: Registration becomes perpetual (no three-yearly renewal) subject to annual fees and compliance; existing agents must upgrade by 31 January 2027
Corporate agents were abolished in favour of brokers
Registration is valid for ten years
Corporate agents must renew registration every year

solution.explanation: Corporate agent registrations are now permanent if annual fees and compliances are maintained, instead of renewal every three years. Existing agents must upgrade by 31 January 2027 (or 31 March 2027 with a late fee). From 1 January 2027 every policy must be linked to the person who solicited it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options misstate the change.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Registration becomes perpetual (no three-yearly renewal) subject to annual fees and compliance; existing agents must upgrade by 31 January 2027

fact_checks.claim: corporate agent registrations are now permanent provided annual fees and compliances are maintained. Previously, they had to be renewed every three (3) years. Existing corporate agents must upgrade to the new perpetual registration by January 31, 2027 (or by March 31, 2027, with a late fee) ... starting January 1, 2027, every policy must be officially linked to the specific person who solicited the insurance policy

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Meena, 32, enrols in PMJJBY for the first time in January through a bank agent. Using the DFS schedule, what premium does she pay, and how much of it goes to the insurer as insurance premium?

options.text: ₹342, of which ₹309 goes to the insurer
₹114, of which ₹103 goes to the insurer
₹436, of which ₹395 goes to the insurer
₹228, of which ₹206 goes to the insurer

solution.explanation: For enrolment in December, January or February (third quarter of the June–May cover), the pro-rata premium is ₹228. It is split as ₹206 to the insurer, ₹15 commission to the BC/agent and ₹7 administrative expenses to the bank.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹436 is for June–August, ₹342 for September–November and ₹114 for March–May.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹228, of which ₹206 goes to the insurer

fact_checks.claim: c) For enrolment in December, January and February – pro rata premium of Rs. 228/- is payable
Rs.228/- collected in the 3rd quarter of risk period: Insurance Premium to LIC/ Insurance Company Rs.206/-; Commission ... Rs.15/-; Administrative Expenses ... Rs.7/-

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about PMSBY claims, based on the Department of Financial Services' FAQs:
I. A disability claim is credited to the bank account of the insured subscriber.
II. If no nominee was registered, the death claim can be filed by the legal heirs.
III. If the insured is missing, the claim is paid after seven years even without evidence of an accident.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Disability claims go to the insured's account; death claims go to the nominee/appointee or, if there is no nomination, the legal heirs. PMSBY covers deaths due to accident confirmed by documentary evidence only, so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Disability claim will be credited in the bank account of the insured bank account holder / subscriber. Death claim will be remitted to the bank account of the nominee / legal heir(s) ... claim can be filed by the nominee/appointee ... or by the legal heir/s in case there is no nomination
PMSBY covers deaths due to accident as confirmed by documentary evidence only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's framework of February 2026, Life Cycle Funds (target-maturity, glide-path funds) may be launched with what tenure?

options.text: Minimum 3 years and maximum 25 years, of any length
Minimum 5 years and maximum 30 years, in multiples of 5 years
Minimum 1 year and maximum 10 years, in multiples of 1 year

solution.explanation: Life Cycle Funds are open-ended funds with a target maturity that follow a glide path across equity, debt, InvITs, ETCDs and gold/silver ETFs. They may be launched for 5 to 30 years, in multiples of 5 years, and a mutual fund may have at most 6 such funds open for subscription at a time. The maturity year appears in the name, e.g. Life Cycle Fund 2055.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other tenures do not match the circular.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Minimum 5 years and maximum 30 years, in multiples of 5 years

fact_checks.claim: Mutual Fund may launch Life Cycle Funds with a minimum tenure of 5 years and a maximum tenure of 30 years. Such fund may be launched for tenures in multiple of 5 years and a maximum of 6 funds by a Mutual Fund can be active for subscription at any given point in time

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a rule for Life Cycle Funds under SEBI's February 2026 framework?

options.text: They are closed-ended and listed on stock exchanges
They must follow the benchmark of a Large Cap Fund
The maturity year must appear in the scheme name, and a fund with less than one year to maturity may be merged with the nearest-maturity Life Cycle Fund with unitholders' positive consent
They must invest only in equity until the last year before maturity

solution.explanation: Life Cycle Funds are open-ended, target-maturity funds following a glide path across equity, debt, InvITs, ETCDs and gold/silver ETFs. The name must carry the maturity date (e.g. Life Cycle Fund 2055); when a fund has less than one year left it may be merged with the nearest-maturity fund with positive unitholder consent; and they follow the benchmark framework of Multi Asset Allocation Funds.
solution.why_others_wrong: They hold a glide-path mix, not only equity; they are open-ended; the benchmark is the multi-asset one.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The maturity year must appear in the scheme name, and a fund with less than one year to maturity may be merged with the nearest-maturity Life Cycle Fund with unitholders' positive consent

fact_checks.claim: as each fund reaches less than 1 year to maturity, such fund may be merged with nearest maturity Life Cycle Fund with positive consent from the unitholders

Life Cycle Funds shall follow benchmark framework as prescribed for Multi Asset Allocation Fund. Life Cycle Funds shall include the maturity date in the nomenclature of the scheme, for e.g. Life Cycle Fund 2055

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's February 2026 categorisation, what restriction applies to the debt portion of an Arbitrage Fund?

options.text: Debt exposure is limited to government securities with maturity under one year and repo of government bonds; no InvITs are permitted
It may hold only AA+ and above corporate bonds of any maturity
It must hold only overnight securities
It may hold up to 35% in credit risk bonds

solution.explanation: An Arbitrage Fund must invest at least 65% in equity and equity-related instruments following an arbitrage strategy. Its debt exposure is limited to G-secs with maturity of less than one year and repo of government bonds, and it cannot invest in InvITs.
steps: Debt: G-secs < 1 year + G-sec repo only
solution.why_others_wrong: Corporate bonds, credit-risk paper and an overnight-only rule are not the prescribed limits.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Debt exposure is limited to government securities with maturity under one year and repo of government bonds; no InvITs are permitted

fact_checks.claim: Arbitrage Fund: Minimum investment in equity & equity related instruments - 65% of total assets ... Exposure in debt instruments shall be limited to government securities with maturity less than 1 year as well as repo of government bonds only ... No investment in InvITs permitted

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: SEBI's revised list of debt fund categories (February 2026) includes an 'Ultra Short to Short Term Fund'. What Macaulay duration must its portfolio have?

options.text: Up to 91 days, by residual maturity

solution.explanation: The revised table has an Ultra Short Term Fund (portfolio Macaulay duration 3–6 months), an Ultra Short to Short Term Fund (6–12 months) and a Short Term Fund (1–3 years). A Liquid Fund is defined by maturity of up to 91 days, not by duration.
steps: 6–12 m: Ultra Short to Short Term
solution.why_others_wrong: 3–6 months and 1–3 years are the neighbouring categories; up to 91 days is the liquid fund rule.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Between 6 months and 12 months

fact_checks.claim: Ultra Short to Short Term Fund: Investment in Debt & Money Market instruments such that the Macaulay duration of the portfolio is between 6 months to 12 months
Ultra Short Term Fund: Macaulay duration of the portfolio is between 3 months to 6 months; Short Term Fund: between 1 year to 3 years

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An existing thematic equity fund's portfolio overlaps 74% with the fund house's other equity schemes (other than its large cap scheme) on the date of SEBI's February 2026 circular. Following SEBI's suggested three-year glide path to the 50% overlap limit, to what level should the overlap be brought by the end of Year 2?

solution.explanation: The excess over the 50% limit is 74 − 50 = 24 percentage points. The glide path realigns 35% of the excess in Year 1, a further 35% in Year 2 and the remaining 30% in Year 3. By the end of Year 2, 70% of 24 = 16.8 points has been removed: 74 − 16.8 = 57.2%. Schemes still above the limit after three years must be merged.
solution.why_others_wrong: 65.6% is the Year 1 level; 62% assumes equal cuts of 12 points a year; 50% is the Year 3 level.

fact_checks.claim: For any scheme offering in sectoral/thematic equity category, Mutual Funds shall ensure that no more than 50% of the schemes portfolios would overlap with other equity schemes in sectoral/thematic category and other equity schemes categories except for large cap scheme
Glide path: Year 1 - 35% of the excess overlap; Year 2 - Additional 35%; Year 3 - Remaining 30%; existing schemes to comply within 3 years, failing which they shall be mandatorily merged

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 aims to raise the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping in cargo movement from 6% to what level by 2047?

solution.explanation: The scheme incentivises a modal shift from rail and road to raise the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047. The Budget also proposed 20 new National Waterways over five years, starting with NW-5 in Odisha.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other targets are not in the Budget.

fact_checks.claim: A Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme to be launched for incentivising a modal shift from rail and road, to increase the share of inland waterways and coastal shipping from 6% to 12 % by 2047

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the Union Budget 2026-27 proposals, up to when can a taxpayer revise an income tax return?

options.text: Up to 30 September of the next year, with a 10% fee
Up to 31 July of the next year
Up to 31 December, as before, without any fee
Up to 31 March, on payment of a nominal fee, instead of 31 December

solution.explanation: The time available for revising returns is proposed to be extended from 31 December to up to 31 March, with payment of a nominal fee. The timeline for filing returns is also to be staggered.
solution.why_others_wrong: 31 December was the earlier deadline; the other dates are not in the Budget.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Up to 31 March, on payment of a nominal fee, instead of 31 December

fact_checks.claim: Extend time available for revising returns from 31st December to upto 31st March with payment of nominal fees

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: To reduce litigation, the Union Budget 2026-27 proposed that taxpayers may update their returns even after reassessment proceedings have started. On what condition?

options.text: Only if the reassessment notice is withdrawn first
Paying tax at an additional 10 percentage points over the rate applicable for that year
Paying 100% of the tax as additional income tax
Paying a flat penalty of ₹1 lakh

solution.explanation: Taxpayers will be allowed to update returns even after reassessment has been initiated, at an additional 10 percent tax rate over and above the rate applicable for the relevant year. Paying 100% of the tax as additional income tax is the condition for immunity in cases of misreporting.
steps: Updated return after reassessment → applicable rate + 10%
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no flat ₹1 lakh penalty or need to withdraw the notice; 100% additional tax is the misreporting immunity condition.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Paying tax at an additional 10 percentage points over the rate applicable for that year

fact_checks.claim: Taxpayers will be allowed to update their returns even after reassessment proceedings have been initiated, at an additional 10 percent tax rate over and above the rate applicable for the relevant year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What did the Union Budget 2026-27 propose about Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDS)?

options.text: Making ICDS mandatory for all companies from 1 April 2026
Replacing Ind AS with ICDS for listed companies
A joint committee of MCA and CBDT to fold ICDS requirements into Ind AS, with separate ICDS-based accounting done away with from tax year 2027-28
Extending ICDS to individuals with business income above ₹50 lakh

solution.explanation: The Budget proposed a Joint Committee of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs and CBDT to incorporate ICDS requirements into Ind AS itself, so that separate ICDS-based accounting ends from tax year 2027-28.
steps: MCA–CBDT committee → ICDS inside Ind AS → no separate ICDS accounting from TY 2027-28
solution.why_others_wrong: The Budget removes, rather than extends, separate ICDS accounting.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A joint committee of MCA and CBDT to fold ICDS requirements into Ind AS, with separate ICDS-based accounting done away with from tax year 2027-28

fact_checks.claim: A Joint Committee of Ministry of Corporate Affairs and Central Board of Direct Taxes to be constituted for incorporating the requirements of Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDS) in the Indian Accounting Standards (IndAS) itself. Separate accounting requirement based on ICDS will be done away with from the tax year 2027-28

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) was launched in April 2025. What did the Union Budget 2026-27 do to its outlay?

options.text: Raised it to ₹22,919 crore from ₹10,000 crore
Raised it to ₹40,000 crore from ₹22,919 crore
Merged it into India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 with no separate outlay

solution.explanation: ECMS, launched in April 2025 with ₹22,919 crore, had its outlay raised to ₹40,000 crore to capitalise on momentum. ISM 2.0 was announced separately.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other figures and the merger are not in the Budget.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Raised it to ₹40,000 crore from ₹22,919 crore

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A company that has moved to the new tax regime has a tax liability of ₹80 lakh for tax year 2026-27 and brought-forward MAT credit of ₹30 lakh accumulated till 31 March 2026. Under the Union Budget 2026-27 proposal, how much credit can it set off this year?

options.text: Nil, because MAT credit lapses from 1 April 2026
₹20 lakh, paying ₹60 lakh and carrying ₹10 lakh of credit forward

solution.explanation: Brought-forward MAT credit can be used only by companies in the new regime, and only up to one-fourth of the tax liability: ¼ × 80 = ₹20 lakh. The company pays 80 − 20 = ₹60 lakh, and ₹10 lakh of credit remains for later years.
solution.why_others_wrong: Full set-off ignores the one-fourth cap; old credit does not lapse; the cap is one-fourth, not one-third.
solution.final_answer: Option C: ₹20 lakh, paying ₹60 lakh and carrying ₹10 lakh of credit forward

fact_checks.claim: Set-off of brought forward MAT credit to be allowed to companies only in the new regime. Set-off using available MAT credit to be allowed to an extent of 1/4th of the tax liability in the new regime ... The brought forward MAT credit of taxpayers accumulated till 31st March 2026, will continue to be available to them for set-off as above

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In BE 2026-27, tax devolution to the States is ₹15.26 lakh crore (₹13.93 lakh crore in RE 2025-26) and the Centre's gross tax revenue (GTR) is ₹44.04 lakh crore, while the States' share has been retained at 41% of the divisible pool. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Devolution falls, since the 41% share applies only to direct taxes
Devolution grows about 13.3% and is about 41% of GTR
Devolution grows about 9.5% and is only about 35% of GTR, because cesses, surcharges and collection costs are outside the divisible pool
Devolution grows about 9.5% and is exactly 41% of GTR

solution.concept: Divisible pool versus gross tax revenue
solution.explanation: Growth: (15.26 − 13.93) ÷ 13.93 ≈ 9.5% (₹1.33 lakh crore more). Share of GTR: 15.26 ÷ 44.04 ≈ 34.7%. The 41% applies to the divisible pool, which excludes cesses and surcharges (and cost of collection), so devolution is a smaller share of gross tax revenue.
steps: 41% is of the divisible pool, not GTR
solution.why_others_wrong: 41% is not applied to GTR; 13.3% misreads the ₹1.33 lakh crore increase; devolution rises and covers all shareable taxes.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Devolution grows about 9.5% and is only about 35% of GTR, because cesses, surcharges and collection costs are outside the divisible pool

fact_checks.claim: In BE 2026-27, tax devolution to the States is estimated at ₹15.26 lakh crore compared to ₹13.93 lakh crore in RE 2025-26 ... ₹1.33 lakh crore more than tax devolution of RE 2025-26
In BE 2026-27, Gross Tax Revenue (GTR) is estimated at ₹44.04 lakh crore ... SFC has recommended for retaining the share of devolution to the States at 41 per cent of divisible pool

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under CGTMSE's CGS-I, what concession in the Annual Guarantee Fee is given to women, SC/ST, PwD, Agniveer and transgender entrepreneurs?

solution.explanation: These target groups get a 10% discount on the guarantee fee. Similar 10% concessions are given for geographic categories (NER, J&K, Ladakh up to ₹50 lakh, Aspirational Districts, ICDDs) and for ZED-certified MSEs, subject to a maximum total of 30%.

questions.question_text: What is the maximum extent of CGTMSE guarantee cover for an MSE located in the North East Region or the UTs of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh?

solution.explanation: MSEs located in the North East Region and the UTs of J&K and Ladakh get 80% cover (75% applies to 'all other' borrowers). An MSE in an RBI-identified credit deficient district gets 5 points more.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under CGTMSE's CGS-I, for claims lodged on or after 1 April 2023, up to what outstanding amount may a lending institution waive the initiation of legal proceedings before invoking the guarantee?

solution.explanation: Initiation of legal proceedings is normally a pre-condition for a claim. The waiver threshold rose from ₹50,000 (2018) to ₹1 lakh (October 2021), ₹5 lakh (January 2023) and ₹10 lakh for claims lodged on or after 1 April 2023.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹50,000, ₹1 lakh and ₹5 lakh were earlier thresholds.

fact_checks.claim: In respect of claims lodged on or after April 01, 2023, the threshold for waiver of legal action has been increased to ₹10,00,000/-

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a condition under CGTMSE's CGS-I?

options.text: New lending institutions get a 10% fee discount in their first year
Claims are allowed even if the account is classified as a wilful default
Credit facilities above ₹50 lakh must be internally rated by the lending institution and be of investment grade
Every guaranteed loan must be backed by collateral of at least 25%

solution.explanation: All proposals above ₹50 lakh must be internally rated by the MLI and be investment grade. Loans are collateral-free (a hybrid model covers only the unsecured part); newly registered MLIs are placed at a 70% risk premium for at least a year; and fraud/wilful-default accounts are ineligible for claims.
solution.why_others_wrong: CGS-I covers collateral-free credit; new MLIs pay a 70% risk premium, not a discount; wilful-default accounts cannot claim.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Credit facilities above ₹50 lakh must be internally rated by the lending institution and be of investment grade

fact_checks.claim: All proposals for sanction of guarantee approvals for credit facilities above ₹50 lakh will have to be rated internally by the MLI and should be of investment grade
MLIs newly registered/which do not have sufficient history of transactions under CGTMSE will be placed at 70% risk premium for a period of atleast 1 year
The accounts classified by the Lending Institution as Fraud / Willful defaulter / Non-Co-operative borrower shall not be considered eligible for Claim Settlement

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank charged CGTMSE's standard fee rate obtains a guarantee of ₹1.5 crore for a women-owned small enterprise. The standard Annual Guarantee Fee for the above ₹1–2 crore slab is 0.85% a year. What is the first-year fee, and on what amount is the fee charged in later years?

options.text: ₹1,14,750 (0.765%); later years on the original guaranteed amount
₹1,27,500 (0.85%); later years on the original guaranteed amount
₹1,02,000 (0.68%); later years on the outstanding amount
₹1,14,750 (0.765%); later years on the outstanding amount

solution.explanation: Women entrepreneurs get a 10% concession: 0.85% × 0.9 = 0.765%. First-year fee = 0.765% × ₹1.5 crore = ₹1,14,750, charged on the guaranteed amount. From the second year the AGF is charged on the outstanding amount (for term loans, as on 31 December).
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1,27,500 ignores the concession; later fees are on the outstanding, not the original amount; ₹1,02,000 deducts 20%.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹1,14,750 (0.765%); later years on the outstanding amount

fact_checks.claim: Slab Above 1-2 crore: Standard Rate 0.85 ... AGF will be charged on the guaranteed amount for the first year and on the outstanding amount for the remaining tenure of the credit facility
Women entrepreneurs/ SC/ST/ Person with disability (PwD) / Transgender Entrepreneur would be given the discount of 10%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the restructured PM SVANidhi scheme approved in August 2025:
I. Coverage is to be extended beyond statutory towns to census towns and peri-urban areas in a phased manner.
II. The Department of Financial Services is responsible for access to loans and credit cards through banks and financial institutions, along with MoHUA.
III. The third loan tranche was raised to ₹75,000.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: I is correct: coverage extends to census towns and peri-urban areas in phases. II is correct: MoHUA and DFS share responsibility, with DFS handling loans and credit cards. III is wrong: the third tranche stays at ₹50,000; only the first two were raised (to ₹15,000 and ₹25,000).
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Coverage expansion: extended beyond statutory towns to census towns and peri-urban areas, in a phased manner

The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) and the Department of Financial Services (DFS) share responsibility. DFS handles access to loans and credit cards through banks and financial institutions
Third tranche: unchanged at Rs. 50,000

questions.question_text: On 25 October 2026 the Prime Minister inaugurated RBI's new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute. Where are they located?

solution.explanation: The Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute are in Bhubaneswar. The Data Centre will house RBI's mission-critical systems including RTGS and NEFT, and the Institute will build expertise in cybersecurity, AI and emerging technologies.

Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran Ltd
Reserve Bank Information Technology Pvt Ltd

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Master Direction on Note Sorting Machines (October 2026), when is a banknote 'fit' for recycling?

options.text: When it is genuine, clean enough for its denomination to be readily ascertained, and passes every fitness parameter
When it belongs to any series ever issued by RBI
When it is genuine, whatever its physical condition
When it passes at least seven of the ten fitness parameters

solution.explanation: A fit note is genuine and sufficiently clean for its denomination to be readily ascertained. Each fitness parameter (soiling, limpness, dog-ears, tears, holes, stains, graffiti, folds, decolouration, repair) is evaluated individually, and a note must pass all of them. Notes of a phased-out series are unfit.
steps: Genuine + clean + passes all parameters → fit
solution.why_others_wrong: Passing some parameters is not enough; condition matters; phased-out series are unfit.
solution.final_answer: Option A: When it is genuine, clean enough for its denomination to be readily ascertained, and passes every fitness parameter

fact_checks.claim: A fit note is a note that is genuine, sufficiently clean to allow its denomination to be readily ascertained and thus suitable for recycling. An unfit note is a note that is not suitable for recycling because of its physical condition or belongs to a series that has been phased out ... A note must pass all the fitness parameters to be considered fit for recycling

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 10 October 2026, RBI opened a special window from 12 October 2026 for which entities, and for what?

options.text: The three public sector oil marketing companies (IOCL, HPCL and BPCL), to meet their entire daily dollar requirements through sale of USD by RBI via designated banks
Public sector banks, to borrow dollars from RBI for FCNR(B) redemptions
All exporters, to sell dollars to RBI at a fixed rate
State governments, to borrow against their gold reserves

solution.explanation: RBI decided to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL by selling USD to them through designated banks, from 12 October 2026 until further notice. This takes their large demand out of the market.
steps: What: RBI sells USD through designated banks
solution.why_others_wrong: The window is for the three PSU OMCs' dollar purchases, not exporters, banks or States.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The three public sector oil marketing companies (IOCL, HPCL and BPCL), to meet their entire daily dollar requirements through sale of USD by RBI via designated banks

fact_checks.claim: Reserve Bank of India has decided to open a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), viz. Indian Oil Corporation Limited, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited ... The facility will come in effect from October 12, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's circular of 2 September 2026, how often and by when must regulated entities report the relief measures they extend in areas affected by natural calamities?

options.text: Annually, with the audited balance sheet
Monthly, by the 7th of the next month, by e-mail
Half-yearly through the CIMS portal, within 30 days of the half-year's end (by 30 October and 30 April)

solution.explanation: The revised framework (effective 1 July 2026) requires REs to submit relief-measure data on the CIMS portal half-yearly, within 30 days of each half-year: by 30 October for the half-year to 30 September and by 30 April for the half-year to 31 March.
solution.why_others_wrong: Monthly, quarterly and annual reporting are not what the circular prescribes.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Half-yearly through the CIMS portal, within 30 days of the half-year's end (by 30 October and 30 April)

fact_checks.claim: REs to submit data relating to relief measures extended in areas affected by natural calamities through the CIMS portal on a half-yearly basis ... The return shall be submitted within 30 days from the end of each half-year, i.e., by October 30 for the half-year ending September 30, and by April 30 for the half-year ending March 31

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: After the MPC's decision of 7 October 2026, at what rate does RBI provide the Standing Liquidity Facility (collateralised liquidity support) to Primary Dealers?

options.text: At the revised repo rate of 5.50%

solution.explanation: The MPC raised the policy repo rate by 25 basis points from 5.25% to 5.50%. The SLF to Primary Dealers is available at the repo rate, i.e. 5.50%, with immediate effect.
solution.why_others_wrong: MSF and SDF rates and Bank Rate + 1% are not the SLF rate.
solution.final_answer: Option B: At the revised repo rate of 5.50%
